title: Adaptive eviction heuristic regression during model rollout — capacity surge action plan
creator: Asha Mehta
summary: During a staged model rollout on 2026-02-04 we observed a sustained memory growth in prefix/KV cache leading to OOMs on several Dedicated nodes and a transient capacity surge affecting customer latency. Initial alerts pointed to eviction miss rates spiking and background compaction lagging. This ticket tracks the incident follow-up: fixes, telemetry, and regression guards.
impact: 3 Dedicated GPU pools experienced OOM restarts, ~12 production services reported >3x P95 latency for 15-40 minutes. No persisted data corruption observed; several customer requests were served by degraded fallback models during the window.
timeline: 2026-02-04 03:14 UTC — Canary rollout of model v3.2 to a subset of nodes
2026-02-04 03:20 UTC — Alert: total cache memory on cluster gpu-dedicated-eu exceeded 85% with rising trend
2026-02-04 03:23 UTC — Autoscaler triggered additional pods but OOMs and restarts continued
2026-02-04 03:35 UTC — Failover to fallback model configuration applied; latency improved slowly
2026-02-04 04:10 UTC — Incident mitigated via emergency rollback of rollout and manual cache compaction
2026-02-04 05:00 UTC — Post-incident collection of heap profiles, eviction logs, and kernel traces started
detection: Anomaly detector on cache memory growth and an internal eviction-miss rate alert fired. Customer reports and enhanced latency dashboards confirmed user impact. Heap profiles showed sustained resident set growth tied to non-evicted prefix entries during bursty write patterns.
root_cause: A regression in the adaptive eviction heuristic (introduced in commit 7b3a2f) changed eviction scoring such that recently-prefetched prefix entries were temporarily pinned when the system saw a high write burst from a model shard. This hysteresis prevented timely eviction. Combined with delayed async compaction (compaction scheduler starvation under high IO), eviction misses accumulated and memory pressure escalated until nodes restarted.
mitigation_done_during_incident: Rollback of the v3.2 model rollout to eliminate the burst pattern on the affected nodes
Manual triggering of full cache compaction on affected nodes
Applied temporary throttle on prefetch to reduce write amplification
Redirected traffic away from overloaded Dedicated pools to Hosted fallback paths
proposed_long_term_fixes: Patch adaptive eviction heuristic to include a time-decay factor that prevents pinned prefetched entries from blocking reclamation under sustained write bursts — owner: Liam O'Connor — estimate: 5 pts
Add a soft cap + load-shedding for prefetching during rollout windows to avoid write amplification — owner: Priya Kapoor — estimate: 3 pts
Fix compaction scheduler priority inversion so async compaction can't starve under high IO — owner: Markus Chen — estimate: 5 pts
Add deterministic canary workload that simulates bursty shard writes during model rollouts (integration test) — owner: SRE team — estimate: 4 pts
Introduce an emergency eviction override API to force synchronous reclamation on a node for on-call use — owner: Runtime infra — estimate: 3 pts
telemetry_and_alerting_changes: Create eviction-latency and eviction-miss percentiles on a per-tenant basis and add alerts at the 95th/99th percentiles — owner: Observability — estimate: 2 pts
Add heap-growth early-warning rule using resident set derivative over 5m and 30m windows — owner: Observability — estimate: 2 pts
Instrument prefetch and pin counts per prefix key namespace and expose in console per-route breakdown — owner: Console team — estimate: 3 pts
testing_and_release_guards: Add a unit/regression test that simulates sustained bursty writes to validate eviction score decay behavior — owner: Runtime QA — estimate: 2 pts
Gate adaptive eviction heuristic behind runtime feature flag for 2 releases with telemetry enabled — owner: Platform releases — estimate: 1 pt
Require model rollout smoke test that runs the canary workload before traffic percentage increase — owner: Product — estimate: 2 pts

ENG-142532 — Implement time-decay eviction scoring and add unit tests (Liam) — due 2026-02-26
ENG-142533 — Fix compaction scheduler starvation path and add e2e stress test (Markus) — due 2026-03-02
ENG-142534 — Build canary burst simulator and add to rollout pipeline (SRE/Priya) — due 2026-03-05
ENG-142535 — Update incident runbook to include emergency eviction override and rollback checklist (On-call lead) — due 2026-02-18
decisions: Do not re-enable the adaptive eviction heuristic by default until telemetry shows zero regression for two weeks in canary — agreed 2026-02-06
Prioritize compaction scheduler fix before heuristic re-rollout — agreed 2026-02-08
Require a maximum prefetch cap during any model rollout window until load-shedding is implemented — agreed 2026-02-10
risks_and_open_questions: Time-decay parameters risk under-eviction if set too aggressive — needs benchmark sweep
Emergency eviction override could cause transient latency spikes; need to document SLO implications
Canary workload coverage for all tenant access patterns unknown — SRE to propose initial coverage matrix
